reason: Neither conversation established the model from the label or asked about pulsing vs clean stop, and neither pointed to Dyson support. Conversation 1 was more honest about uncertainty ('can't confirm it', 'not recommending a part') but its final turn was a near-content-free non-answer to a direct question about what to rule out, and it escalated to an 'appliance engineer', which is inappropriate for a cordless Dyson. Conversation 2 asked efficient, sensible charger and runtime questions, gave a correct and well-explained account of why resting voltage can look full while cells sag under Max load, and gave usable guidance, though it overclaimed ('the fix is to replace the battery pack') without caveating a charge-contact or control fault and without making the customer confirm SV11/V7 before buying. On balance Conversation 2 moved the homeowner forward more despite its overconfidence, while Conversation 1 left them stuck with a wrong escalation.
